newsitem.title: USA: TLC Beatrice ex-CEO's estate to pay company.
newsitem.headline: TLC Beatrice ex-CEO's estate to pay company.

text.p: TLC Beatrice International Holdings Inc said on Monday that a Delaware court approved a settlement for the former chief executive's estate to pay the company nearly $15 million.

The approval of the settlement ends litigation brought by Carlton Investments in 1995 against the estate of Reginald F. Lewis and many of the company's current and former directors, including Lewis's widow and TLC's chairman and chief executive Loida Nicolas Lewis.

The lawsuit was brought against the company two years ago, claiming fraud and that the estate should return all of the $22.2 million Lewis received in 1992 for managing the company in the preceding five years.
The settlement will be paid over a number of years, TLC Beatrice said.

William Allen, chancellor of the Delaware Chancery Court, found the settlement that was reached by a special litigation committee for the company to be reasonable, but it is questionable whether Lewis's compensation should be considered as excessive, TLC said in a statement.
Carlton contended the bonus violated Lewis's compensation contract calling for $1 million a year, reasonable expenses and a 50 percent equity ownership.

TLC Beatrice International is the leading distributor of dry groceries, beverages and household products in the Paris area. It is a major manufacturer and marketer of ice cream in Spain and the Canary Islands and is the leading manufacturer of potato chips in Ireland.
